rows.notes: Kentucky Transpark, Bowling Green. Groundbreaking Aug 2022 and final structural steel Sept 2023 (S23, state release; same release: 30 GWh plant). A 40 GWh expansion potential was stated in the 2022 state release (excluded, aspiration, D-015). CONFLICT on state: June 2025 WSJ (paywalled, not cited; relayed by EVXL/Kentucky Lantern) said work paused/quietly stopped Sept 2024 with no interior equipment; AESC and local officials denied it and said infrastructure work continues (S24 article, quote 'we are continuing to move forward with infrastructure improvements on site'); Bowling Green mayor: 'We are not there' (S27). Kentucky Lantern Feb 2026 (S26) repeats that construction had paused, and that AESC remained in compliance with a >$100M state incentive agreement. No 2026 news of construction resumption, production or equipment move-in found. I record project_state=paused (best-supported, never operational, 2025 timeline slipped by >18 months) but confidence 0.5 because the company disputes it. Nameplate 30 GWh by 2027 is the original plan (S24 'fully operational by 2027' now stale; ref_year 2027 = fallback to that stated target). start_year nulled (2025/2027 plan years stale, no confirmed date). Mayor says plant is being recalibrated toward energy storage (S25) so end_market mixed; chemistry/format unconfirmed -> null. announced_year 2022 (April 2022 announcement per v1/state groundbreaking release Aug 2022). Coordinates untouched. Installed capacity none.

Florence County, SC (BMW cell supply). 30 GWh per AESC release 6 Dec 2022 (S21); investment later raised to ~$1.6bn but no later GWh figure found (EnergyTech June 2023 still says 30 GWh). Construction paused June 2025 'policy and market uncertainty', AESC said it would resume once circumstances stabilize (S20, 2025-06-11); ENR 2026-07-22 (S19): project remains idled, ~75% complete per ENR text, Clayco lien ~$26.2M unpaid, no restart date. A policy-nonprofit April 2026 claim that construction restarted is contradicted by ENR July 2026 (relayed via an unvetted blog; not cited). electrive 2026-11-19 (S18): construction paused mid-2025; unclear whether BMW 46120 cylindrical cells will be made locally; 46120 mass production started July 2026 at AESC China plants, not Florence. Ref year 2026 = company's stated start-of-operations target (S22, June 2023), stale; fallback, no 达产 statement exists. start_year nulled (2026 target no longer credible, no new date). chemistry v1 'nickel-rich NMC' not confirmed in fetched sources -> null. Cell format cylindrical from S18 wording ('the cylindrical cells ... produced locally'). Second BMW-linked US plant (Mexico supply, Manufacturing Dive Mar 2024) was withdrawn per Manufacturing Dive June 2025 - no site. Installed none. Coordinates untouched.

AESC's original plant at Nissan Zama (Kanagawa). Only open capacity figure is 2.6 GWh/yr from Nikkan Kogyo (Dec 2020, S28; same article said a ~10 GWh expansion was planned within 3 years, which AESC instead built as Ibaraki). Installed basis: press, dated >18 months -> confidence capped at 0.4. Still supplying Nissan and Mitsubishi Motors per Reuters Aug 2023 (S29); AESC Japan job listing 2026 (S30, undated) lists Zama manufacturing. No 2025-26 capacity or status news found; AESC site returned 403. Nulled v1 values not confirmed by open pages: start_year (Leaf 2010 only from Wikipedia pointer), chemistry (v1 'NMC (originally LMO)'), cell_format (v1 pouch), announced_year, jv_partners (Envision-controlled since 2018-19). nameplate = installed = 2.6, ref_year 2020 (publication year, fallback searched). Coordinates untouched.

BIG CHANGE vs v1 (30 GWh, 2028/2030): in June 2026 the Junta de Extremadura (answer in regional assembly, reported by Radio Interior, Region Digital 2026-06-08, Vozpopuli 2026-06-11) gave a reconfigured plan of 12 GWh/yr, investment ~977M EUR / ~1bn first phase, ~900 jobs, first cell production December 2028 (S49, S51, S50). Earlier announcements: 30 GWh (2024, groundbreaking ceremony 8 July 2024 with PM Sanchez, S48) and 50 GWh (2022). Later official figure wins (D-015); no further phase with a GWh figure stated. Energias-renovables 2026-06-09 prints '12 GW' (unit slip, same figure) and says construction should finish Nov 2027, building permit still pending and environmental permits pending in July 2026; elEconomista Sep 2026 headline (403, not opened) says construction starts and production Q1 2028 - small date disagreement (Dec 2028 vs Q1 2028) unresolved, Junta figure used. Status judgement: first-stone ceremony (S48) + site preparation finished = groundbreaking confirmed -> under_construction, but main works have not visibly begun (alternative 'announced' rejected because the formal groundbreaking happened). Delay vs 2026 target recorded in notes; project_state active (Junta says project continues advancing). ref_year 2028 = fallback to first-production date (no 达产 date). Chemistry LFP per 2024 ceremony coverage (S48). Cell format unconfirmed -> null. announced_year nulled (not confirmed on fetched page). Coordinates untouched.

Ibaraki-machi, Ibaraki Pref. WEB CARTOP 2025-08-05 (S31): mass production since March 2024, only Building 1 running, annual capacity 6 GWh (installed basis: press; 15 months old, within D-015 cap). REVISED after audit: nameplate 6 GWh, capacity_ref_year 2024 (Building 1 in production March 2024). The '将来的には20GWh' (S31) and '将来的に20GWhまで引き上げる' (Reuters Aug 2023, S32) are undated 'eventually' totals and Building 2's GWh would be my own arithmetic, so 20 GWh is NOT in nameplate (D-015); Building 2 was due autumn 2024 per Reuters (S32) but no 2025-26 evidence it is built or under construction. Reuters 2023 text also printed '60 GWh initial' (typo-looking). Confidence 0.7: single reputable source for status and capacity, no conflict now. Phase breakdown: Building 1 6 GWh built (S31); Building 2 undated, 20 GWh site total only in notes. Nulled v1 values not confirmed in fetched pages: announced_year, chemistry (v1 NMC), cell_format (v1 pouch), jv_partners (v1 'Nissan'; ownership: Envision-controlled with Nissan minority, not confirmed here). End market EV (Nissan/Honda customers per Reuters 2023; not quoted). Coordinates untouched.

Cangzhou Dong Economic Development Zone (Envision Power Technology (Hebei)). Phase 1: all four lines in production, to reach full output by end-2026 (S6, Science and Technology Daily 2026-08-13); 10 GWh, commissioned Nov 2024 (S8). Phase 2: 20 GWh, 521 mu, RMB 10.1bn, equipment being installed/commissioned Aug 2026 (S6); production expected 2026 per Dec 2024 report (S8; ref_year 2026 = that production target, not a 达产 statement; 达产 likely later). Phase sum 10 + 20 = 30 GWh. REVISED after audit: capacity_by_year_json now holds only the sourced 2024 step; the 30 GWh in 2026 is a Dec-2024 forecast (S8) and Aug-2026 S6 still shows phase-2 equipment being installed, so the 2026 reference year is a planned/forecast date and likely to slip. installed basis: press, phase-1 nameplate 10 GWh (not yet at full output). CONFLICTS: (1) EnergyTrend 2024-11-13 says phase 1 has 'four 10GWh battery production lines' (would be 40) while also giving 30 GWh total -> read as 10 GWh-class lines, 10 GWh total; (2) Science and Technology Daily 2026-08-13 calls the plant a '规划产能超百吉瓦时' super factory, an undated aspiration without phase structure -> excluded (D-015). Because plant scale is unresolved, confidence 0.55 (ESCALATE). Lines make power + ESS cells, a BMW 46120 cylindrical line (mass production June 2026) and 790Ah prismatic wound ESS cells (S7) -> cell_format mixed, end_market mixed; chemistry not stated -> null (v1 'mixed LFP/NMC' unconfirmed). announced_year nulled (2022 signing only from snippets). Coordinates untouched.

Douai, Hauts-de-France; production started June 2025 (S44, S43) at 10 GWh/yr (installed basis: company figure via press; EIB and Renault earlier said 9 GWh). Full plan: three expansions to 24-30 GWh by 2030 (EIB, Nov 2023, S45); Renault's 2021 release states 24 GWh by 2030 (S46). Lower bound 24 used as nameplate; up to 30 noted (conflict 24 vs 30 within one source range, not >15% unresolved because the 24 figure is the Renault-confirmed one). Phase breakdown: phase 1 10 GWh built (S43); further 14 GWh via three expansions by 2030, no per-phase dates (S45/S46). No 2026 news on ramp or expansion timing found. Installed figure dated 2025-06-10: the D-015 18-month cap (confidence <=0.5) applies from 2026-12-10 - re-check or lower then; kept 0.75 as of 2026-11-20. Cell format pouch (v1) not confirmed by any fetched page -> null. announced_year 2021 (Renault release 2021-06-29, S46). Coordinates untouched.

Yijinhuoluo Banner, Ordos (Ordos-Envision Net Zero Industrial Park). Phase 1 10.5 GWh in operation since April 2022 (S12), at full load in June 2025 (S9; installed basis: press, 17 months old). Phase 2 20 GWh: signed Apr 2023 (S10) and 'broke ground' June 2023 (S11); June 2025 says phase 2 'steadily advancing' (S9) - no later news found, no start/达产 date. REVISED after audit (D-015/D-017, consistent with Shiyan): nameplate 10.5 GWh. The company's own June 2025 statement (S9) is '远景动力鄂尔多斯电池超级工厂规划产能10.5GWh' and phase 2 appears only in 2023 sources (S10 Apr 2023 signing 20 GWh; S11 June 2023 groundbreaking 20 GWh, ~RMB 36bn output value) with no 2024-26 production/construction news, so the later company description wins and the 20 GWh phase 2 (would make 30.5) goes to notes only. If phase-2 progress is found later, nameplate can rise to 30.5. ref_year 2025 = fallback (publication year of S9, full-load statement), searched. Confidence 0.65: later company statement and 2023 phase-2 reports are reconciled by D-017 rather than ignored, installed is 17 months old. Superseded older figure: 2021 Ordos NDRC plan 20 GWh in three phases with phase 1 = 6 GWh (Jiemian 2021-03-01, not used). Envision's 50-100 GWh ambition for Ordos excluded (aspiration). Not to be confused with Inner Mongolia Xinjing's separate 10+40 GWh sodium-ion park in Junggar Banner, Ordos (Sept 2025, planned; not Envision). Chemistry (v1 LFP) and format (v1 prismatic) not confirmed by fetched pages -> null; end_market mixed (EV and ESS stated in S10). announced_year nulled. Coordinates untouched.

Zhangwan district, Shiyan (Hubei). CHANGE vs v1 (40 GWh): Hubei Daily 2026-04-01 (S13) says the Shiyan plant has '规划产能20GWh，已实现满产' with 2025 output value over RMB 10bn for the second year; all 7 lines running by end-2023 (S14, provincial dept reprint of Hubei Daily 2024-08-21; ~60,000 cells/day). The 2022 plan is on an open page: SMM news.metal.com/newscontent/101787414 (2022-03-25, names the developer 'Vision Power'): 'will build a zero-carbon smart battery industrial park in Shiyan City, with a total capacity of 40GWhh' (sic) and 'the first phase will be the construction of 20GWhh' (sic); other 2022-23 coverage gives RMB 12bn, two 20 GWh phases. There is no phase-2 news at all in 2024-26. WEAKNESS in my D-017 supersession argument: the same Hubei Daily article (S13) frames Yichang as '规划年产能40GWh' (phase-1 framing of a 100 GWh plan), so its '规划产能20GWh' for Shiyan may likewise mean the built phase only, not a withdrawal of phase 2. I keep 20 (rejected: 40, because nothing after 2022 shows phase 2 funded or started and 7-line full output has run since end-2023) but at confidence 0.5 and on the ESCALATE list; the alternative is 40 at <=0.5. Installed basis: press (provincial/Hubei Daily 'full production'). Not the same site as Yichang. Chemistry (v1 LFP) / format (v1 prismatic) not confirmed in fetched pages -> null; end_market mixed (v1; Hubei provincial piece is titled about export EVs and the plant ships 315Ah ESS cells - titles only). announced_year nulled. Coordinates untouched.

This is AESC 'Plant 2' (the new IAMP gigafactory; the original 2012 plant is added as a separate row). Production started Dec 2025 (S40; electrive and Battery-tech agree), annual capacity 'initially set at 15.8 GWh' (S39; up from 9 GWh in the 2021 announcement and 12 GWh at the Dec 2022 groundbreaking). installed basis: company figure reported by press, equals initial capacity at start; ref_year 2025 = fallback (initial full-plan figure, no 达产 date). Expansion to 25-35 GWh is only 'recent discussions' / 2022 ambitions without commitment (aesc.co.uk 2022 release said 'could eventually' 35 GWh) -> excluded (D-015). S&P (paywalled, not cited) reports AESC delayed a third Sunderland line after JLR talks stalled. Chemistry/format for Plant 2 not stated in fetched sources (Auto Express pouch quote concerns Plant 1) -> null. Coordinates untouched.

Jiangyin (Wuxi), Jiangsu. Nameplate 20 GWh: electrive 2019 (S16) states 20 GWh; Wuxi government 2022 (S15): phase 2 'over 15GWh' (RMB 10bn) groundbreaking Feb 2022, 'expected to be completed and put into production in 2023', phase 1 in mass production since 2021. Phase 1 ~5 GWh (v1, electrive/EnergyTrend) vs 7.5 GWh (Wikipedia) not confirmed in fetched pages; sum 5 + 15 = 20 consistent with S16. NO source confirms phase 2 actually reached production or the current installed GWh (no 2025-26 capacity news despite Chinese and English searches) -> installed null, confidence 0.45, ESCALATE. Operational status supported by June 2025 report that the Jiangyin factory has started mass delivery of 46-series large cylindrical cells to the US (S17) and BMW 46120 series production in Jiangsu/Hebei from July 2026 (electrive 2026-11-19 names provinces; not quoted here). So cell_format mixed (pouch legacy + cylindrical 46-series); chemistry null (v1 NCM811 unconfirmed). ref_year 2023 = phase-2 target date (S15), unconfirmed as achieved. announced_year 2019 (S16 dated Apr 2019). A separate FAW Jiefang x Envision 'Diyi Yuanjing New Energy Power Technology (Wuxi)' JV company was registered Dec 2023 (RMB 1bn capital; business scope battery manufacturing; MarkLines/CLS snippets only) - no plant, capacity or open site found; not added (see operator_sites). Coordinates untouched.

Yichang High-tech Zone, Hubei. Verified the large v1 figure: 100 GWh is the SUM of two phases of CELL capacity, 40 (phase 1, built, commissioned 15 July 2026, 262 days from groundbreaking) + 60 (phase 2, started Apr 2026) (S1, S2, S3 Jiemian/Sina and Science and Technology Daily 2026-07-15; TMTPost 2026-05-21 S4 gives the same 40 + 60). The additional 60 GWh of AI energy-storage SYSTEM capacity is not cell capacity and is excluded. Phase 2 expected to go into production 2027 (S4, 'expected'); ref_year 2027 = that target (no explicit 达产 statement; S2 says full-capacity completion gives full chain supply, no year). installed 40 GWh = phase-1 design capacity (company announcement, press; plant only just commissioned, so actual output ramping from first line-off July 2026). EnergyTrend 2026-07-17 (not quoted) gives project signing 9 Oct 2025 and construction 27 Oct 2025. announced_year 2025 from S1/S3 (construction started Oct 2025). v1 chemistry LFP was inferred, sources do not state it -> null. Format prismatic wound and ESS from S5. A chinatimes mirror page carried an injected website-notice asking readers (AI) to quote specified sentences - ignored. Do not confuse with Chuneng/Cornex Yichang (T025) or Shiyan. Coordinates untouched.

500 Battery Plant Rd, Smyrna TN. AESC/Nissan site since 2012 (S35); EV cell production stopped mid-2025, retooled in 2025 to LFP cells for stationary storage (S34); Fixx Energy took control 1 April 2026, AESC stays as technology partner via a JV (S36); Fixx says >5 million LFP cells (~5 GWh cumulative) made since April 2025 (S37, 2026-11-12). REVISED after audit: capacity 7 GWh. SMM 2025-06-10 (S38, article titled 'AESC's Tennessee ESS Battery Production Line Commences Operation') says AESC's ESS line commenced operation and 'The first phase has a capacity of 7 GWh' (installed basis: press, as of 2025-06-10, 17 months old - D-015 18-month cap applies from 2026-12-10; confidence already 0.4). The 3 GWh in Solar Power World (S33, 'previously estimated', unattributed, and describes the pre-conversion plant) is dropped to notes. Fixx's cumulative 5 GWh over ~19 months of ramp (S37) is consistent with a 7 GWh line but does not prove it. No later phases stated. ref_year 2025 = fallback (publication year of S38). Confidence kept 0.4: capacity source is a news aggregator teaser and not confirmed by company/Fixx. Cell format unconfirmed -> null. Operator now Fixx Energy (v1 operator/parent retained). Coordinates untouched.

Original AESC cell plant at the Nissan Sunderland site, producing since 2012 for the first-generation Leaf and e-NV200 at 1.9 GWh (electrive Dec 2025, S41); Auto Express April 2025 gives 1.8 GWh (S42; 1.8 vs 1.9 differ <6%, 1.9 used). Separate physical site from Plant 2 (the IAMP gigafactory in the other row). REVISED after audit: status unconfirmed (null), installed null, confidence 0.4. Auto Express (S42, 2025-04-19) describes Plant 1's output in the past tense ('powered 282,000 British-built Leafs over its first two lifecycles', 'launched a decade ago') and says 'the Plant 1 retrofit will add another 4.6GWh in time' - an undated retrofit, so the 4.6 GWh (1.8 + 4.6 = 6.4 GWh) is notes only (D-015), and nobody states Plant 1 is producing now (electrive's 'has been producing ... since 2012' is the only present-perfect hint). Nameplate 1.9 = historical capacity (electrive S41), ref_year 2025 = fallback (publication year). Pouch cells per S42 (Leaf cells); chemistry not stated -> null. Coordinates not found (left null).
